title: Apache Kafka
summary: Design a distributed commit log: partitioned append-only segments on disk, leader-follower replication with an in-sync replica set, and consumers that track their own offsets.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Producers append messages to named topics; consumers read in order
Many independent consumer groups; replay from any offset
Retention by time/size; optional compaction by key
Millions of messages/s per cluster; low ms latency
No loss of acknowledged messages when a broker dies

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: At 2 GB/s ingest with replication factor 3, the network carries about 6 GB/s of writes. The design has to be sequential I/O end to end.

produce(topic, key, value, headers) -> (partition, offset)      acks = 0 | 1 | all
fetch(topic, partition, offset, maxBytes) -> records[]
commit(group, topic, partition, offset)
subscribe(group, topics) -> partition assignment via group coordinator

head: Concept
What it is
rows: Named stream, split into P partitions
Ordered append-only log; unit of parallelism and ordering
Partition stored as files of ~1 GB: `00000000000005000000.log` + `.index` (offset → byte position) + `.timeindex`
Monotonic position of a record in its partition

blocks.text: Only the active segment is written; old segments are immutable, so retention just deletes whole files and compaction rewrites them in the background.

blocks.caption: Leaders take writes; followers replicate; the controller manages metadata

items: Producer partitions by hash(key), batches records per partition, sends to the partition leader.
Leader appends to its log; followers fetch from the leader (pull replication).
With `acks=all`, the leader replies once all in-sync replicas have the batch.
Consumers fetch from leaders (or nearby followers), process, commit offsets.

sections.title: Deep dive: replication and the ISR

items: Each partition has a leader and RF−1 followers. The **ISR** is the set of replicas caught up within `replica.lag.time.max.ms`.
**High watermark** = highest offset replicated to all ISR members; consumers only see up to it.
`acks=all` + `min.insync.replicas=2` + RF=3: a write succeeds only if at least 2 copies have it; one broker can die with no loss.
If ISR shrinks below min.insync, producers get errors instead of silent data loss (availability traded for durability).
Leader election picks from the ISR; `unclean.leader.election=false` forbids electing a stale replica.
Leader epochs let a returning replica truncate divergent entries.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Durability comes from acks=all with min.insync.replicas=2 on replication factor 3: we can lose a broker and still never lose an acknowledged message.

items: Sequential append to the OS page cache; disks do what they're best at.
Zero-copy `sendfile` from page cache to socket for consumers.
Batching and compression (lz4/zstd) per batch, end to end — brokers don't decompress.
Consumers pull at their own pace; no per-message acks on the broker.
Sparse offset index makes seeks cheap.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Tiered storage moves old segments to S3 so brokers keep only recent data on local disks.

sections.title: Deep dive: consumer groups and exactly-once

items: Within a group each partition is owned by one consumer; max parallelism = partitions.
Rebalances reassign partitions when members join/leave; cooperative sticky assignment avoids stop-the-world.
Idempotent producer: (producer ID, sequence number) per partition lets the broker drop duplicates on retry.
Transactions: atomically write to several partitions and commit consumer offsets — exactly-once for read-process-write within Kafka.
External side effects still need idempotent consumers.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Controller elects new leaders from ISR in seconds
Better key, more partitions, salt hot keys
Scale consumers up to partition count; alert on lag
Plan partitions to throughput; KRaft raises limits

items.title: Requirements
items.text: Append, read in order, replay, retention.

items.title: Non-functional
items.text: Millions/s, no acked loss, per-key order.

items.title: HLD
items.text: Partition leaders, followers, controller quorum, consumer groups.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: ISR + high watermark, sequential I/O, exactly-once.

items.q: How many partitions should a topic have?
items.a: Target throughput ÷ per-partition throughput (producer and consumer side), plus headroom; increasing later breaks key→partition mapping.
Keep the latest value per key forever (changelogs, state snapshots); tombstones delete keys.

items.q: How does a consumer find offset N?
items.a: Pick the segment by base offset, binary-search the sparse index for the nearest position, scan forward.
Kafka is a retained, replayable log with partition ordering; RabbitMQ is a broker with routing and per-message acks for task queues.

items: Partition = ordered append-only log in ~1 GB segments.
RF 3 + acks=all + min.insync 2 = no acked loss.
High watermark: consumers read only fully replicated data.
Speed: sequential I/O, page cache, zero-copy, batching.
One consumer per partition per group.
Idempotent producer + transactions = EOS inside Kafka.
